pricing.billing_basis: duration of audio streamed, including silence and retries; rate-dependent estimate, not an invoice; the pricing page's streaming example uses $0.01 per minute but its regional table is not published as text, and the Turbo preview names no separate rate

protocol_caveat: Amazon Transcribe Turbo is in public preview: AWS routes standard streaming requests for supported languages in us-east-2 (Ohio) to it with no API change, so there is no model parameter and the service does not name the model; identity rests on the endpoint and region. The WebSocket API is used directly: a SigV4-presigned URL on port 8443, audio as AudioEvent messages in AWS's binary event-stream encoding, results as TranscriptEvent messages keyed by ResultId and final when IsPartial is false. There is no finalize command mid-stream, so the bench's silence tail is sent and then an empty AudioEvent ends the stream; completion is the service closing the socket after its last results. End-of-turn detection (semantic turn-taking) is off. The default quota is 25 concurrent streams per Region. Latency from regions far from Ohio is not comparable.
